newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up at or near intraday highs on Friday on short-covering at lower levels, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 21,220 yuan ($2,560) per tonne, rising 440 yuan. It opened at 21,090 yuan and hit a low of 20,950 yuan per tonne.
August rose 250 yuan to 20,800, September 270 to 20,920, October 410 to 21,110, December 420 to 21,220 and the January 1997 contract 430 to 21,200 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 81,820 tonnes from 74,980 tonnes.
Copper opened higher on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and rose steadily with most contracts closing at or near their intraday highs.

LME copper explored higher numbers in the afternoon after finding support below $2,300 a tonne in the morning. Three months copper turned back, however, at around $2,325/30 and ended the day $13 firmer at $2,318.
"Many investors took advantage of the LME gains to liquidate the short positions they built a few days ago," one trader said.
"Investors did not want to hold large positions with the approach of the weekend, which was another factor encouraging them to take profits while they could," he added.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices were around 20,900 yuan per tonne with demand still sluggish, traders said.
Traders said with speculative funds dominating trading, price fluctuations could be expected in the short term.

"A lot of hot money poured into the metal market two weeks ago, and that led to wide-range movements which will extend into next week, especially with speculative funds still hovering around the market," another trader said.
August rose 100 yuan to 13,950, September 190 to 14,150, October 300 to 14,250, November 320 to 14,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 4,510 tonnes from 4,580 tonnes.
